**Finding: missing (medium severity) — transition assistance and data return absent.**

**What I found.** This is a site development and hosting agreement where HDI holds materially all of our operational data: it stores and operates the Site (§1.4), generates order export files and processes our inventory imports (§1.5), and is expressly exposed to our "Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information" (§8.1).

Despite that, Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) covers only the renewal/notice mechanics, the Termination Date, and our obligation to pay HDI a Termination Payment. There is no transition, exit, wind-down, migration, or data return/deletion language anywhere in the document — searches for "return" and "customer data" surfaced nothing on point, and §10.7 (Survival) preserves only §§6.3, 7, 9 and 10. Notably the asymmetry runs against us: we owe an eight-quarter Termination Payment on exit but get no contractual right to our own data back or any help standing the Site up elsewhere.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted a new Section 4.3 after §4.2(c), tracking the playbook's preferred position:

- (a) up to six (6) months of reasonable transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, including migration cooperation;
- (b) return of all Content, user information, customer data, order data and Confidential Information within thirty (30) days in a commonly used, machine-readable format;
- (c) deletion thereafter with written certification.

I placed it in Section 4 rather than creating a new section so the obligation sits with the existing termination mechanics and inherits the defined "Termination Date." The comment flags the fallback (90 days of assistance, same 30-day export) in case HDI pushes back on the six-month tail.
